classification.difficultyReason: Infer the large diameter from adjacent semicircular cut-outs, then subtract their areas.

content.prompt: Two semicircles, of radii $3\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$, are cut from a larger semicircle, as shown opposite.

spec.description: An upper semicircle contains adjacent upper semicircular cut-outs along its diameter, smaller on the left. Their diameters meet and together span the outer diameter. Black replaces ordinary source blue outlines; light purple identifies the remaining region and red dots identify the cut-out centres.
spec.mathematics: Cut-out radii are 3 cm and 5 cm. Their diameters partition the large diameter. The outer radius is not labelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no inferred radius or area is supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the radius of the largest semicircle?

answer.worked:
The two smaller diameters together form the largest diameter.

$$\begin{align*}D&=2\times3+2\times5\\D&=16\text{ cm}\\R&=\frac{16}{2}\\R&=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the approximate value of the remaining area? Use $\pi\approx3.14$.

answer.short:
$47.1\text{ cm}^2$

Subtract the areas of both smaller semicircles from the largest semicircle.
answer.worked:
Subtract both cut-out areas from the largest semicircle.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\pi\times8^2-\frac12\pi\times3^2-\frac12\pi\times5^2\\A&=32\pi-\frac92\pi-\frac{25}{2}\pi\\A&=15\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A&\approx15\times3.14\text{ cm}^2\\A&\approx47.1\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
